plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, PLTU, MSFU) to zero for capital preservation.
Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and meet single-name limits.
This plan significantly reduces overall portfolio leverage and concentration.
It prioritizes stability and lower drawdown over aggressive growth.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation, targeting a modest ~1.5%/month. It significantly de-risks the portfolio by eliminating leveraged ETFs and reducing concentration. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more limited upside potential.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, PLTU, MSFU) to reduce overall leverage.
Increase QQQ exposure to 17% to balance the portfolio with broad index growth.
This plan reduces concentration and brings leveraged ETF exposure within limits.
It blends growth potential with a more controlled risk profile.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets risk-first growth, aiming for ~2.5%/month. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while maintaining exposure to quality tech and broad market. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with a reasonable growth outlook.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, PLTU, MSFU) to press growth.
Add to QQQ to 19% to maintain a strong broad market presence.
This plan leans into leverage and concentration for higher potential returns.
It requires strict stop discipline due to amplified risk and daily decay.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets stretch growth, aiming for ~4%/month. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware that this raises both upside and drawdown potential, leveraged ETFs decay daily, and it can lose a lot fast. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, PLTU, MSFU) to near zero.
Increase QQQI to 30% to prioritize steady monthly distributions.
This plan focuses on low drawdown and reliable income over growth.
It aims to park cash for yield, reducing high-beta single names.
income.read: This income plan targets steady monthly distributions, aiming for ~1%/month. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income by rotating into income/covered-call ETFs and cutting high-beta names. Remember, distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
